assumptions: The supplied packet is sufficient to score without additional questions; all candidate-specific commercial metrics remain unvalidated unless explicitly evidenced.
The initial beachhead is in-scope Polish or nearby EU importers with material CBAM exposure, rather than the exempt majority of small importers.
The founder does not perform accredited verification or regulatory filing and procures specialist input only as a prepaid add-on.
The proposed prices, delivery-hour ranges, margins, CAC, renewal, and 7-10 year wealth path are targets rather than demonstrated results.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: The most valuable evidence would be several paid diagnostics from importers above the threshold, documenting budget owner, sales cycle, fully loaded CAC, delivery and support hours, realized contribution margin, and quantified savings or avoided work versus defaults, broker bundles, CBAMable, and SAP. At least one paid monitoring renewal, signed data-use and retention rights, measured referral-channel conversion, and evidence that reusable mappings improve delivery economics would materially strengthen the score.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The redesign identifies a real decision created by certificate-bearing CBAM: whether the incremental value of actual verified emissions exceeds collection and assurance cost. Focusing on importer-controlled shipment data avoids dependence on owning supplier measurements. The insight is useful but readily discoverable by brokers, software vendors, and enterprise platforms.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Certificate exposure at published EU ETS-linked prices and a named buyer's use of an external CBAM solution establish genuine compliance and financial pain. However, no evidence shows willingness to pay for this distinct diagnostic, its proposed price, or which internal budget owner buys it; default values can also reduce the necessity of the service.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Fixed scope, advance billing, capped support, and prepaid specialist work are sensible controls and could support a capital-light service. Yet every decisive economic input is unvalidated: price, CAC, sales cycle, labor, specialist and insurance cost, margin, payback, and renewal. A £199-£699 monthly software benchmark makes the proposed premium dependent on unproven managed value, while the path to 5 million PLN relies on substantial customer count and retention.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: In-scope importers with material certificate exposure form a clear segment, and a Poland or CEE starting point is geographically coherent. The 50-tonne exemption removes the vast majority of importers and concentrates demand in fewer, larger accounts, while the packet provides no count or addressable-spend estimate for the regional beachhead.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: An integration-neutral decision service may occupy a narrow advisory gap, but it lacks contracts, exclusive access, channel ownership, regulated authority, or a proprietary control point. CBAMable, brokers, and SAP can add or bundle comparable exposure analysis, making segment domination unlikely on current evidence.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Importer workflow access could support adjacent exposure monitoring, declaration readiness, supplier-data triage, and other trade-carbon workflows across EU geographies. Expansion is plausible but speculative because the initial customer relationship, repeat use, retained-data rights, and transferable workflow advantage are not established.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Potential retained mappings and benchmarks could modestly improve delivery, but legal reuse rights are unsigned and switching costs, proprietary data coverage, and learning-rate effects are unproven. Core rules are public, source data and verification are externally controlled, agreements are nonexclusive, and incumbents can copy or bundle the workflow.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A fast independent default-versus-actual analysis could save unnecessary supplier collection and verification effort, and the productized-service format may be more accessible than enterprise software. No quantified speed, cost, accuracy, certificate saving, or UX advantage has been shown against broker advice, low-priced software, SAP, or internal analysis.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The definitive regime began in 2026, certificate prices create measurable exposure, and first definitive declarations create immediate preparation needs. This is a strong regulatory trigger, although the same timing is attracting capable incumbents and simplification has narrowed the customer base.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Targeted lists and paid diagnostics provide a testable founder-controlled route, with accountants, customs advisers, and associations as plausible referral sources. No pipeline, response rate, conversion, channel agreement, CAC, or sales-cycle evidence exists, and concentrated larger accounts may require trust-heavy enterprise selling that is difficult part-time.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data modeling skills, modest capital requirement, and fixed-scope delivery fit a part-time launch. Material risks remain in regulatory accuracy, liability, cybersecurity, specialist review, multilingual data quality, enterprise sales, and keeping delivery within 15-25 weekly hours; these are manageable to test but not yet demonstrated as manageable at scale.

highest_value_structural_change: Secure a repeatable direct distribution and workflow position through a signed partnership with a customs adviser, accounting network, or trade association that supplies qualified in-scope importers while preserving the candidate's direct paid relationship and permission to retain anonymized mappings. This would address the weakest structural point—customer acquisition—while creating data accumulation and switching benefits that generic outbound alone does not provide.
main_structural_strength: The offer converts a mandatory, financially measurable regulatory event into a fixed-scope importer decision product and deliberately removes open-ended supplier chasing and accredited verification from the base service, improving controllability, capital efficiency, and founder fit.
primary_score_limiter: There is no demonstrated reason importers will buy and renew a separate premium service rather than use defaults, internal staff, brokers, low-priced CBAM software, or SAP; consequently distribution, realized economics, and a durable workflow position are all unresolved at once.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The combined substitute evidence is most damaging: CBAMable already offers supplier evidence, audit history, regulatory export, and broker white-labelling for £199-£699 per month, while SAP can bundle customs, ERP, supplier-emissions, reporting, and financial-liability workflows. Together with permitted default values, this undermines both premium willingness to pay and resistance to bundling.
